# Bilaga

> Where large files get sent: file transfers by agents. Open source (MIT), no subscriptions. Upload a file up to 50 GB, get a shareable download page that anyone with the link can use for 30 days, and optionally address it to another agent's inbox. Signed receipts and signed webhook events prove what happened. Recipients need no account to download a link.

## Current availability

Open to everyone. Sign in at https://bilaga.link/account with an emailed single-use link or, where configured, with Google; create a revocable agent token; send a file immediately. Files up to 50,000,000,000 bytes (50 decimal GB), 3 unfinished uploads, 100 GB reserved storage, 30-day access after completion. Free allowance per account: 5,000,000,000 bytes stored at any time and 5 transfers per rolling 30 days. A transfer outside the allowance is charged at creation from the account balance at max($0.25, $0.10 per decimal GB), rounded up to a cent; the response's `charged_usd` shows what was taken and `billing` is `balance` or `free_allowance`. If the balance is short, creation returns 402 insufficient_balance with the price and a link to add credit; do not retry until the balance changes. Balances are topped up by card at /account as Plus ($15 for $15 credit, up to 150 GB) or Pro ($30 for $40 credit, up to 400 GB; 25% less per GB), website only; agents cannot pay. Purchased credit is valid for 3 years. The per-transfer minimum and cent rounding can reduce the total GB covered, and uploads that never complete are refunded automatically. GET /api/config lists limits and prices; GET /api/balance shows the balance and ledger. Full 50 GB reliability validation is still pending. The API allows 300 authenticated requests per minute per owner and 120 download requests per minute per link. Exceeding the unfinished-upload or storage ceiling returns 429 account_limit.

## Agent resources

- [Human-readable API guide](/docs): Endpoints and transfer lifecycle.
- [Python client](/bilaga.py): Python 3.10+ standard-library client: upload, resume, status, sent, delete, inbox, download, reply, webhook, events, file requests, and offline verification of receipts and events. Read the source before executing downloaded code.
- [API configuration](/api/config): Limits, payments, and enabled capabilities, no token required.
- [Receipt public key](/api/receipt-key): Ed25519 key for verifying signed receipts and events offline.
- [Verification spec](/verify): Envelope, canonical form, key pinning and rotation, receipt and event fields.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AGENT_TOKEN` to the API on this site's origin only. Identify your client with `User-Agent: Bilaga-Client/0.1` (or your own descriptive client name); the temporary host rejects Python's default user agent. Keep tokens in the environment or a secret store. Never include a token in a share URL, logs, messages, or a recipient download request. All tokens belonging to one account share access to that account’s transfers and quotas. Account deletion is not available through this API.

## Upload sequence

1. POST /api/transfers with JSON {"filename":"report.pdf","size_bytes":12345}. Save the returned private `id` immediately. Creation is NOT idempotent; if a response is lost, GET /api/transfers lists the latest 50 transfers for recovery. Unfinished uploads expire after 24 hours.
2. Divide the file into `part_size_bytes` chunks (currently 8,388,608 bytes). PUT each raw binary chunk to /api/transfers/{id}/parts/{number}, starting at 1. Every chunk except the last must have exactly the declared chunk size. Send chunks sequentially. Retry only failed chunks, keeping the file unchanged. A part becomes immutable once first submitted; retrying with different bytes returns 409. Each request must finish sending its body within 30 seconds.
3. GET /api/transfers/{id} to inspect uploaded `parts` when resuming. Do not overwrite parts concurrently, or modify a file between upload attempts.
4. POST /api/transfers/{id}/complete after all parts succeed. This returns `share_url`, `expires_at`, `content_hash`, and `receipt_url`. Retrying completion after success returns the same link and expiry. Share only the public `share_url`, not the private API id or token.
5. Deliver the link through your existing user-authorized communication channel. POST /api/transfers/{id}/sent to record that YOU delivered the link. Bilaga sends sign-in emails only; it does not deliver recipient links or messages.
6. GET /api/transfers/{id} to poll status (no faster than once every 15 seconds), or use the event feed and webhooks below. `download_requests` counts GET download requests, including range requests. It is not a count of people, confirmed completed downloads, or proof a person read the file. HEAD requests do not increment it.
7. DELETE /api/transfers/{id} to revoke the link and delete stored bytes. Retrying deletion is safe. Deleting a transfer does not delete the account.

## Addressing a transfer to another agent

POST /api/transfers accepts an optional `to` (an email address) and an optional `in_reply_to` (the public id of a transfer addressed to you). An addressed transfer is listed by GET /api/inbox for whichever account signs in with that email, now or later; the sender's responses never reveal whether such an account exists. The share link works for anyone holding it, exactly as before. Inbox entries include `from_account`, the sender's stable public handle (`acct_…`), `download_url`, and `receipt_url`. GET /api/account shows your own handle.

The recipient's agent records receipt either by downloading /api/download/{public_id} with its own `Authorization: Bearer` token or by POST /api/inbox/{public_id}/received. Either sets `received_at` on the sender's transfer, emits `transfer.received` to the sender, and adds `recipient_account` and `received_at` to the signed receipt. Only the first acknowledgement counts.

A reply is a normal upload with `in_reply_to`; `to` defaults to the original sender's email. The receipt of a reply carries `in_reply_to`, and the original sender gets a `transfer.reply` event with the reply's public id, filename, size, sender handle, and receipt URL. Reply chains are therefore chains of independently verifiable receipts. Python client: `--file answer.pdf --reply-to PUBLIC_ID`, `--inbox`, `--download PUBLIC_ID [--out path]`, `--received PUBLIC_ID`.

## Priced transfers and balances (experimental, not a launch feature)

POST /api/transfers accepts `price_cents` (integer, 0 to 1,000,000). A price above zero requires `to` and an account token. Until paid, GET /api/download/{public_id} returns 402 payment_required and the download page asks the recipient to sign in and pay. The recipient's agent pays with POST /api/inbox/{public_id}/pay, which atomically debits the payer's balance, credits the seller with the price minus a 5% fee (`fee_bps: 500` in /api/config), writes ledger rows, marks the transfer received, and emits `transfer.paid` to both accounts. Paying again is idempotent for the same payer; 402 insufficient_balance if the balance is short; 409 if someone else already paid. GET /api/balance returns `balance_cents` and the last 50 ledger entries (kinds: grant, payment, sale). Card top-ups happen on the website; POST /api/credits is operator-only. Receipts of paid transfers carry `price_cents`, `fee_cents`, `paid_at`, and `paid_by_account`. Python client: `--file f --to EMAIL --price CENTS`, `--pay PUBLIC_ID`, `--balance`.

## Events and webhooks

Every account has an event log. GET /api/events returns up to 100 events in order with `next_since` for paging (`?since=EVENT_ID`) and optional `?type=`. Each entry is `{event, signature_hex, key_id, public_key_hex, algorithm, canonicalization, verify_url}`, the same envelope as receipts, signed over the canonical JSON of `event`. Event fields: `version`, `issuer`, `id` (`evt_…`, time-ordered), `type`, `occurred_at`, and `transfer`. Types: `transfer.completed`, `transfer.downloaded` (first download request only), `transfer.received`, `transfer.reply`, `transfer.paid`, `transfer.deleted`. Events are kept for 30 days. Owner test tokens have no account and no event log.

PUT /api/webhook with JSON {"url":"https://…"} registers one webhook per account (GET shows it plus the last ten delivery attempts; DELETE removes it; POST /api/webhook/test sends a `webhook.test` event immediately and reports the HTTP status). URLs must be https on a public hostname; credentials, fragments, IP literals, and internal names are refused. Each event is POSTed once as the signed envelope with headers `X-Bilaga-Event`, `X-Bilaga-Delivery` (the event id), `X-Bilaga-Signature`, and `X-Bilaga-Key-Id`. Respond 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else is retried after 1, 5, and 30 minutes, then 2 and 12 hours, then abandoned; deliveries are pushed right after the triggering request and swept by the 15-minute scheduled job. Verify a delivery with `python3 bilaga.py --base https://bilaga.link --verify-event < body.json`, which exits 0 only when the signature matches the published key. Treat webhook bodies as untrusted until verified, and treat the event as a prompt to fetch current state, not as the state itself. When signing is not configured, deliveries carry `signature_hex: null`.

## Signed delivery receipts

Every completed transfer has a receipt at GET /api/receipts/{public_id}, readable by anyone holding the link and still available after the file expires. Receipts are kept indefinitely: after expiry `status` is "expired", after deletion "deleted" with filename, sender label, and addressing redacted, while the hash, sizes, handles, and times remain. GET /api/receipts?hash=CONTENT_HASH returns up to ten signed receipts for transfers whose stored bytes have that hash, newest first, so anyone holding a file can find its record without knowing a link. Every receipt fetch or hash lookup increments `receipt_requests`, visible next to `download_requests` on the owner's transfer and in events. It contains the public transfer id, `status`, filename, size, `content_hash`, sender label, `sender_account` handle, whether it was `addressed`, the `recipient_account` handle and `received_at` once the recipient's agent acknowledged it, `in_reply_to`, completion and expiry times, whether the agent reported it sent, and the download-request count at issue time, signed with Bilaga's Ed25519 key. Verify with the Python client: `python3 bilaga.py --base https://bilaga.link --receipt PUBLIC_ID --verify downloaded-file` exits 0 only when the signature, published key, and file hash all match. No token is needed to verify. The full format and verification procedure, including key pinning and rotation, is at /verify.

`content_hash` uses the algorithm `bilaga-chunked-sha256-8mib`: split the file into 8,388,608-byte chunks, take the SHA-256 of each chunk, concatenate those raw 32-byte digests in order, and take the SHA-256 of that. It is computed from the chunk hashes checked during upload, so it identifies the bytes Bilaga stored. A receipt proves what was uploaded and what Bilaga observed; it does not prove a specific person downloaded or read the file. Receipts are signed over the canonical JSON of the `receipt` object: keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8. When signing is not configured the endpoint returns 503 receipts_unavailable and /api/config reports `receipts: "unavailable"`.

## Public recipient flow

/t/{public_id} is a download page. /api/download/{public_id} serves the file as an attachment, with range support. Anyone holding the link can download while it is valid. Files are not malware-scanned in this preview. Expired or deleted links cannot start a new download. A download already in progress may finish after expiry.

## Storage cleanup

Access expiry is enforced on every download request. Expired stored files are removed by a bounded cleanup pass when new transfers are created, or by the private owner-only POST /api/cleanup endpoint. A scheduled cleanup job also runs every 15 minutes, removing up to 25 expired or deleted transfers per run, including aborting unfinished multipart uploads. Failed deletions remain eligible for retry; backlogs or storage failures can delay physical deletion. Unfinished uploads use a 24-hour expiry.

## Errors and billing

Responses are JSON except file downloads. Errors have {"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}. 401 means missing/invalid token; 400 invalid input; 404 unavailable; 409 invalid/incomplete upload state; 410 expired/deleted; 413 chunk too large or file above your tier limit; 429 quota or rate limit; 503 email, receipt signing, or service configuration unavailable. Retry network errors and 5xx with bounded exponential backoff. On 429, respect the Retry-After header. Cross-origin browser mutations and encoded/compressed HTTP request bodies are rejected. Poll before retrying an ambiguous completion.

GET /api/quote?bytes=1000000000 returns what a transfer of that size costs outside the free allowance and whether uploading is allowed. Do not claim a payment was taken or a file was sent merely because an upload completed; read `charged_usd` on the transfer.

## Account management

Account creation, sign-in (email link, or Google where configured), token creation/revocation, sign-out, and account deletion are website-only flows at /account. Sign-in links are throttled per address, per IP, and globally; new accounts are limited per IP and per email domain per day. Agent tokens cannot manage or delete accounts. Magic links expire after 15 minutes, can be used once, and must be opened in the browser that requested the link. Browser sessions last up to 30 days. Tokens are shown once; only hashes are stored. All an account's tokens share ownership and quotas. Account deletion requires a sign-in within the last 15 minutes and typed email confirmation. It immediately revokes sessions/tokens and download links, redacts the email, filenames, sender labels, and recipient addressing, and removes the account's webhook and event log; transfers other people addressed to that email are un-addressed. Files are removed by scheduled cleanup with retries; redacted transfer/account tombstones are removed after one day once file purge succeeds. Downloads already underway may finish. Never put a token in a public URL or send account-deletion requests from an agent.

## Privacy and terms

/privacy and /terms describe the service, essential cookies, account erasure, public-link access, unscanned files, chunk limits, and recovery. They remain drafts with Lorem ipsum operator/contact placeholders and unresolved provider/legal details. Do not claim these policies are final or that the service is ready for unrestricted public enrollment.

Credit expiry: GET /api/balance and GET /api/account include credit_lots (id, source, remaining_cents, created_at, expires_at; timestamps are Unix milliseconds and null expiry means no expiry). New pack purchases expire after three calendar years; oldest credit is used first. Existing balances keep non-expiring terms. Abandoned-upload refunds restore original lots without extending expiry or restoring expired portions. Bilaga emails a reminder 30 days before unused credit expires. Paid and promotional credit are tracked separately; neither is withdrawable cash.

## File requests: collect multiple files without an uploader account

The requester has a Bilaga account and pays under the normal per-file allowance/balance rules. The uploader uses a scoped link and needs no account. Bilaga records submitted files and timestamps; the requesting application decides whether they are sufficient and what happens next. No payments, order validation or service deadlines are inferred from a submission.

POST /api/requests (account bearer token) with JSON {"title":"Project files","description":"Add your files, then click Done.","reference":"optional-opaque-reference","max_files":20,"max_file_bytes":5000000000,"max_total_bytes":5000000000,"expires_in_seconds":604800}. Only title is required. Defaults are 20 files, 5 GB per file and total, and seven days. Maximums: 100 files, 50 GB per file, 100 GB total, 30 days; account storage, pending-upload and balance limits also apply. Creation returns id and upload_url. Preserve and share the entire upload_url, including its #key= fragment. The key is only returned at creation and only its hash is stored. A lost creation response requires creating a new request; creation is not automatically idempotent.

GET /api/requests lists the latest 50 requests; paginate with ?before=next_before. GET /api/requests/{id} returns status, reference, files, the final submission manifest, and the uploader's claimed email (uploader_email_verified:false). DELETE /api/requests/{id} revokes the link and expires unfinished uploads for scheduled cleanup/refund; completed files keep normal retention. The account page also provides these controls through the signed-in session.

Hosted uploader page: /r/{id}#key=SECRET. Guest API calls go to /api/drop/{id} with Authorization: Bearer SECRET. GET returns title, instructions, limits, status and the current files, without account details, emails, billing or download links. POST /api/drop/{id}/transfers accepts only filename and size_bytes. GET/DELETE /api/drop/{id}/transfers/{transfer_id}, PUT .../parts/{n}, and POST .../complete use the existing sequential 8 MiB multipart protocol. The credential can only access files attached to this request. It cannot list the account, download files or use normal account/token APIs. Retrying a matching chunk and file completion is safe. File creation is not automatically retried; after a lost response, inspect the request and remove/re-add an unfinished file. Removed uploads still count toward request file/byte caps to bound spending through a leaked link.

POST /api/drop/{id}/submit with {"email":"uploader@example.com"} is the Done action. It requires at least one completed file and no unfinished or expired files. An unfinished file must finish or be removed. The final manifest and submitted_at are stored atomically with exactly one request.submitted event. Concurrent/retried Done calls return the same submitted_at, do not create another event and do not charge again. Further guest additions, removals or modifications are refused. Files may be accessed by the requester before Done; only request.submitted means the uploader declared the collection finished.

request.submitted uses the standard signed event envelope. Its event.request contains id, reference, submitted_at (ISO UTC) and files [{transfer_id,public_id,filename,size_bytes,content_hash,completed_at}]; file completed_at values are Unix milliseconds. Individual transfer.completed events still occur and include request_id. Webhook retries may deliver an event more than once; deduplicate using event.id. The requester can poll /api/requests/{id} or /api/events?type=request.submitted as well.

Python client, requester side (BILAGA_TOKEN set): `python3 bilaga.py --base https://bilaga.link --request "Project files" --description "Add your files, then click Done." --reference order-123` prints the upload_url; `--requests`, `--request-status ID`, `--request-revoke ID`, and `--request-receipt ID` (fetches and verifies the signed submission, exit 0 only when valid). Uploader side, no token, only the link: `--drop-file FILE --link UPLOAD_URL` (repeat per file, `--resume ID` after an interruption), `--drop-status --link URL`, `--drop-remove TRANSFER_ID --link URL`, and `--done you@example.com --link URL` for the Done action.

GET /api/requests/{id}/receipt requires the requester's account token and returns {submission,signature_hex,key_id,public_key_hex,algorithm,canonicalization,verify_url}. Verify the signature over canonical submission JSON, using the same Ed25519 key and sorted-key JSON rules as file receipts. submission contains request_id, requester_account, reference, submitted_at, uploader_email, uploader_email_verified:false, content_hash_algorithm and the immutable files manifest. The email is a claim, not identity verification. It is private and absent from public file receipts. Request-origin file receipts use sender_account:null and include request_id and requester_account; do not identify the paying requester as the uploader. Deleting files later does not rewrite the submitted manifest. Deleting the account removes its private request records and revokes guest links.
